migration_flags.title: Three new picking type fields: qc_type_id, store_type_id, xdock_type_id
migration_flags.detail: V19 introduces dedicated picking types for quality-control (lines 78, 1040-1049), storage (lines 79, 1050-1058), and cross-dock (lines 80, 1070-1080) operations. These are separate Many2one fields on stock.warehouse, replacing moves previously handled by the generic internal transfer type. Migration must create these picking types and populate the new warehouse fields.

migration_flags.title: models.Constraint replaces legacy _sql_constraints syntax
migration_flags.detail: Lines 91-98 use models.Constraint(...) for warehouse name and code uniqueness per company. Scripts checking for _sql_constraints must be updated to detect the new constraint API.

migration_flags.title: xdock_type_id has cross-conditional activation logic
migration_flags.detail: Cross-dock picking type active state depends on BOTH reception_steps != one_step AND delivery_steps != ship_only (line 993). This compound condition is new in v19. Existing warehouses upgraded with single-step in either direction will have cross-dock deactivated.

migration_flags.title: _get_receive_rules_dict / _get_receive_routes_values pattern for extending modules
migration_flags.detail: New methods at lines 793-807 and 582-616 provide alternate route/rule data without the initial pull rule for modules (e.g. purchase) that add MTO-triggered receiving. Modules extending stock must migrate from get_rules_dict/_get_routes_values to these variants for purchase flows.

migration_flags.title: External inter-company transit location silently skipped if not found
migration_flags.detail: create_resupply_routes (line 712) silently skips a supplier warehouse if the transit location is missing. Cross-company setups must verify stock.stock_location_inter_company exists before configuring resupply.

migration_flags.title: reception_route_id and delivery_route_id carry ondelete=restrict
migration_flags.detail: Lines 81-82 set ondelete='restrict' on both route fields. Migrations that attempt to delete routes still referenced by warehouses will receive a database integrity error. Routes must be unlinked from warehouses before deletion.

migration_flags.title: _default_name counts archived warehouses for numbering
migration_flags.detail: Line 32 uses active_test=False when counting warehouses for default name generation. Restored databases with archived warehouses will see higher-than-expected default numbering.

key_findings.company_binding: company_id is readonly at field level and protected in write() with UserError; _check_company_auto=True enforces domain filtering on all check_company=True relational fields; name and code constraints are scoped per-company
key_findings.step_change_cascade: Changing reception_steps or delivery_steps triggers: location active toggling, resupply MTO rule adjustment (only when crossing ship_only boundary), picking type activation/deactivation, route name update, and full rule archive-and-recreate cycle
key_findings.route_creation: _get_routes_values returns reception_route_id and delivery_route_id configurations; _create_or_update_route archives old rules and calls _find_existing_rule_or_create to reactivate or create rules; warehouse_selectable routes are added to route_ids M2M
key_findings.mto_rule: mto_pull_id is the MTO pull rule on the global Replenish on Order route; its source, destination and picking type are derived from the delivery_steps routing and updated whenever delivery_steps changes
key_findings.resupply_wh_ids: Resupply route changes are computed as a before/after diff; removed suppliers archive routes, added suppliers unarchive existing or create new inter-warehouse routes; cross-company resupply requires external transit location and sets route company to empty
key_findings.v19_new_picking_types: qc_type_id, store_type_id, and xdock_type_id are new dedicated picking type fields on stock.warehouse in v19; these replace generic internal transfers for quality-control, putaway-to-stock, and cross-dock operations
key_findings.rule_proc_method: First rule in every route always uses make_to_stock; all subsequent chained rules use make_to_order
key_findings.get_rules_dict: Returns Routing namedtuples per step per warehouse; two_steps reception uses store_type_id for push; three_steps reception uses qc_type_id then store_type_id; pick_pack_ship delivery uses pick_type_id pull then pack_type_id push then out_type_id push
